notes: Row n / (2n-1)!! tends to Poisson(1): the k-th factorial moment of the number of short pairs is k! C(2n-k,k)(2n-2k-1)!!/(2n-1)!! = prod_{i<k}(2n-k-i)/(2n-1-2i), in [0,1] and tending to 1; inclusion-exclusion plus dominated convergence give P(S=s) -> e^-1/s!. Core Lean (decide): enumerated matchings give rows n<=5 and the factorial-moment identity for n<=5. Outside Lean: the factorial-moment identity and the limit for general n.

prior_art.note: Young (arXiv:2408.17232, p.1) attributes the factorial-moment limit (hence Poisson) to Kreweras-Poupard 1978; that paper not read directly.
